name: ADP
summary: Payroll, tax filing and HR for small and mid-sized employers, sold as four RUN packages: Essential, Enhanced, Complete and HR Pro. No public pricing anywhere — /pricing is a 404 and every tier on the comparison page says “Get pricing”, so budgeting means a sales call.
best_for: small and mid-sized employers who want payroll, tax filing and compliance handled by the largest and oldest provider in the category: over 75 years, and their own figure of more than 900,000 small businesses on RUN alone. It suits those who would rather have a named account team than a cheaper self-service tool
skip_if: you need to budget before you talk to sales, because you simply cannot: every route ends at a quote form. Also skip it if you are a one-or-two-person company where a published-price competitor covers the same job, and if you only pay 1099 contractors, price that specific product rather than the packages, because ADP sells it separately
honest_knock: The quote-only posture is normal in payroll, so the honest complaint is not that ADP hides its price — it is what that does to you as a buyer. You cannot compare ADP against anyone without first giving a salesperson your headcount and your phone number. And the three-months-free banner carries an end date, which puts a clock on a decision you cannot yet cost. Ask for the per-employee-per-month rate and the per-payroll-run fee separately. Ask what happens in month four. And ask what the price becomes at double your current headcount, because payroll pricing steps rather than scales smoothly. One detail worth noticing: ADP does publish an /llms.txt, a file whose entire purpose is to guide AI assistants around its site. They are willing to machine-readably explain what they sell. They are not willing to say what it costs.

pricing.notes: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) ADP shows no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, and we checked four places before saying so. /pricing returns a 404, and so does /pricing.md. The RUN product page offers only a “Get Pricing” button. And the dedicated package-comparison page lists all four tiers with “Get pricing” under each one and not a single figure. The tiers are Essential Payroll, Enhanced Payroll (adds ZipRecruiter, State Unemployment Insurance and garnishment payments), Complete Payroll & HR Plus (adds basic HR support) and HR Pro Payroll & HR (enhanced HR support and staff perks). A promotion was running when we read it: three months of free payroll, marked “Ends 8/27”, with terms behind an asterisk.

cost_traps.label: Quote-only pricing
cost_traps.evidence: No published price: pricing page and package page return only "Get Pricing" buttons, no figure anywhere (read 15 Aug 2026)

cost_traps.label: Per-seat pricing
cost_traps.evidence: Ask for the per-employee-per-month rate and the per-payroll-run fee separately.

compare_with.name: Gusto
compare_with.why: the comparison that makes the difference visible rather than the features. Gusto publishes its per-month and per-person rates on its own site, so you can cost it in five minutes; ADP will not, so you cannot. If both can do the job, the question becomes what a sales conversation is worth to you — and for a business under fifty people that is usually the whole answer
